title: 0490-realtime-win-probability-and-latent-player
universal_lens: A continuous dominance measure T-score maps discrete game outcomes to stochastic processes enabling real-time win probability via Brownian motion analogies and latent player ability estimation through shared statistical kernels. Diffusion-standardized statistics under high-frequency accumulation converge weakly to Brownian motion; dynamic T-process models game evolution via stochastic functional calculus with linear feature mappings.
gsi_mapping: GSI employs Bayesian inference on T-score processes to update latent player ability estimates using conformal predictive intervals derived from team-level statistical scores and observed game dynamics. Bayesian inference framework encodes win probability as posterior over T-score paths using conformal prediction; incorporates opponent effects via modified T-process and empirical risk minimization.
gse_mapping: GSE utilizes T-process state transitions to model situational awareness, where each play's outcome modifies team and player dominance states through kernel-based flow contributions and dynamic score adjustments. Situational reasoning maps real-time game states to latent player and team dynamics through state-transition kernels; updates belief over T-process paths using sequential filtering and predictive scoring.

primitives.name: T-Score Dominance Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model (a) T-score function T(a,b): [0,∞)2→R mapping scores to continuous dominance, with draw benchmark c satisfying T(x,x)=c and sign(T(a,b)-c)=sign(a-b).
primitives.assumptions: Scores are non-negative reals; T is symmetric around draw; monotonicity preserved under score difference.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When a = b, T(a,b) = c; otherwise, sign of difference determines dominance direction.

layer2.mapping: Maps discrete game outcomes into a continuous stochastic domain for probabilistic win prediction using Brownian motion approximations.
layer2.telemetry: Win probability derived from cumulative distribution of T-process over time.

primitives.name: Team Statistical Score Model
primitives.verbatim_quote: (b) Team model: T^k = α0 + F_α(S^k) + ε^k, IID noise σ2, where α0 ≡ TFS (Team Fundamental Score = pre-game baseline strength) and F_α(S^k) ≡ TSS^k (Team Statistical Score = game-specific performance).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{T}^k': 'team T-score at time k (dimensionless)', '\\alpha_0': 'TFS (baseline strength) (dimensionless)', 'F_{\\alpha}(S^k)': 'TSS (statistical performance) (dimensionless)', '\\varepsilon^k': 'IID noise term (dimensionless)', 'S^k': 'game state vector (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Noise is independent and identically distributed; F_α is deterministic function of S^k.

layer2.mapping: Enables real-time updates of team strength by integrating observed stats into evolving T-score.
layer2.telemetry: Dynamic adjustment of TFS based on residual error between predicted and actual T-scores.

primitives.name: Player Contribution Kernel
primitives.verbatim_quote: (c) Player model: T^k = α0 + Σ_j f_α(S^{k,j}) + ε^k with a COMMON player function f_α (same STATS evaluated the same way across players); PSS^{k,j}=f_α(S^{k,j}); PCS^{k,j} = α0/J + α0·(PSS^{k,j}-TSS^k/J)/D^k ·1{D^k>0}, D^k=Σ_j|PSS^{k,j}-TSS^k/J| — equal-share baseline plus deviation-weighted reallocation of TFS (Σ_j PCS = α0).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{T}^k': 'team T-score at time k (dimensionless)', '\\alpha_0': 'TFS (baseline strength) (dimensionless)', 'f_{\\alpha}(S^{k,j})': 'player contribution (dimensionless)', 'PSS^{k,j}': 'player statistical score (dimensionless)', 'TSS^k': 'team statistical score (dimensionless)', 'D^k': 'deviation sum (dimensionless)', 'J': 'number of players (dimensionless)', '\\varepsilon^k': 'noise term (dimensionless)'}
primitives.assumptions: Common evaluation kernel f_α applies uniformly; total player contributions sum to TFS.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If D^k = 0, PCS^{k,j} reduces to equal share α0/J.

layer2.mapping: Allocates latent player ability via deviation-weighted redistribution of team baseline strength.
layer2.telemetry: Latent player ability estimate via normalized deviation from team average performance.

primitives.name: Interval-on-Fire Flow Index
primitives.verbatim_quote: **Verdict:** ADAPT — adapt the closed-form Brownian-motion win-probability derivation and the "Interval on Fire" (IoF) flow-contribution index design to NFL drive-level data; the basketball linear model itself does not transfer.
primitives.assumptions: Flow index adapts to temporal granularity of drive-level events; Brownian motion analogy holds for win probability evolution.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Applies only when temporal resolution allows meaningful flow tracking.

layer2.mapping: Translates discrete event sequences into continuous-time stochastic flows for win probability estimation.
layer2.telemetry: Real-time win probability updates based on cumulative IoF contributions per time interval.

primitives.name: Dynamic T-process
primitives.verbatim_quote: Dynamic T-process: diffusion standardization S_i(t)=(S̃_i(t)-m_i t)/v_i (note: denominator is v_i, not v_i√t, deliberately matching Brownian variance structure Var∝t); under high-frequency Poisson-type accumulation the standardized STATS converge weakly to Brownian motion (functional CLT).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'S_i(t)': 'standardized statistic process, dimensionless', 'm_i': 'mean rate of accumulation, time^-1', 'v_i': 'diffusion coefficient, time^(-1/2)', 't': 'time, minutes'}
primitives.assumptions: ['High-frequency Poisson-type accumulation of statistics', 'IID mean-zero noise', 'Diffusion-standardized cumulative statistics approximate Brownian motion']
primitives.breakdown_regime: Low-frequency or non-Poisson regimes where convergence fails

layer2.mapping: Maps to GSI's probabilistic forecasting kernel; GSE's state transition model uses this for continuous-time evolution of game metrics.
layer2.telemetry: Convergence diagnostics of standardized statistics to Brownian motion

primitives.assumptions: ['Linear feature mapping F_α', 'Opponent TFS β0 enters additively', 'Brownian noise ε(t) independent of S_j']

reasoning_traces.think: This chapter introduces a framework for modeling real-time win probability in team sports using a continuous dominance measure called the T-score. The core idea is to map discrete game outcomes—such as wins or losses—into a continuous stochastic domain that evolves over time. This enables analytical tractability for estimating win probabilities dynamically during gameplay. The methodology builds upon prior work involving Brownian motion analogies and introduces a novel Interval-on-Fire (IoF) flow-contribution index tailored for temporal granularity. It distinguishes between team-level and player-level models, where the former uses a fundamental score (TFS) and a statistical score (TSS), while the latter allocates latent player ability through a common kernel function applied across all players. The adaptation of these concepts to NFL drive-level data is emphasized, suggesting that while the underlying principles remain valid, specific implementations must account for sport-specific dynamics. The use of empirical datasets from the B.League provides validation for the proposed models, particularly in how they handle minute-by-minute play-by-play data. The framework supports both Bayesian inference for updating latent abilities and conformal prediction for uncertainty quantification in real-time scenarios. reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 3 introduces a foundational framework for estimating win probability through a combination of statistical modeling and player efficiency metrics. It begins with a win rate analysis and proceeds to coefficient estimation using AIC stepwise selection for the Chiba Jets. The model is validated on two held-out playoff games, where path analysis of mT vs PW_t provides strategic insights. Player performance is evaluated using PCS, STATS X, PTS, EFF, and PER rankings, revealing discrepancies between total statistical output and dynamic contribution to win probability. The paper notes that while the model shows high correlation (ρ=0.989) between TFS and win rate, this correlation is circular due to estimation from the same dataset used for validation. Additionally, the formula for PW_t is described as ad hoc, lacking empirical testing of its underlying assumptions such as Brownian motion and linear F_α. This chapter emphasizes the need for rigorous validation and the limitations of relying solely on retrospective data without out-of-sample accuracy metrics like Brier score or calibration curves. reasoning_traces.think: Chapter 4 introduces a layered approach to real-time win probability (WP) modeling, integrating temporal flow intervals (IoF), player involvement indices (X-index), and variance-stabilized regression targets. The IoF mechanism identifies key moments in a game based on momentum shifts, defined by a threshold δ that varies per game. This thresholding is arbitrary yet foundational for identifying active periods. The X-index measures player participation during these IoFs, though it does not distinguish causality—only presence. A major challenge lies in the NFL’s low-event structure, which strains Brownian approximations. To mitigate this, the paper proposes a normalized T-score transformation of final margins, stabilizing variance and enabling better regression performance. The closed-form WP model replaces computationally expensive grids with an analytic expression, calibrated on recent seasons. These primitives collectively enable a robust, scalable system for situational reasoning and predictive analytics in real-time sports environments.
